overview.description: Romanian Tarok is a point-trick game played mainly around Suceava in Moldavia. Introduced from Austria in the 19th century; uses 54-card Austrian tarok pack (22 trumpsâ€”taroaceâ€”plus four suits of eight). Highest trump skiz, then luna (XXI), lowest trump (I). Card values: skiz, luna, lowest trump and Kings 5, Queens 4, horses 3, Jacks 2, others 1. Objective: win tricks with valuable cards. Follow suit; must trump if unable. Cards in tricks counted in groups of three with 2 points subtracted per group. Phases: deal, bidding, calling a king, talon use, trick play, bonuses, declarations. Three-player variant Taper and other regional forms exist.

history.origins: Introduced from Austria in the 19th century; played mainly around Suceava in Moldavia. 54-card Austrian tarok pack; point-trick with call a King; three-player Taper and other regional variants exist.

setup.players: Four players (principal form); three-player variant Taper when a fourth is not available.
setup.deck: 54-card Austrian tarok (22 trumps plus 8 cards in each of four suits: hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades).
setup.dealing: Dealer places first 6 cards face down in the centre as the talon, then deals the remaining 48 cards in batches of 6 so each player receives 12 cards. Deal and play anticlockwise.

rules.objective: Declarer's team wins the hand by taking at least 36 card points in tricks (70 points total in the pack). Opponents win with 35 or more. Card points are counted in groups of three with 2 points subtracted per group.
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal: Six cards to talon, 12 to each player in batches of 6; deal anticlockwise.
2. Bidding: Player to dealer's right speaks first. Bids are unul de doi (take two from talon), unul de unu (take one), or solo (no talon). Pass allowed. Bidding continues until three players have passed.
3. Call king: Declarer must call a king; its holder is declarer's partner (secret until revealed in play). Declarer may call a king they hold (play alone) or if the called king is in the talon (play alone).
4. Talon: In doi declarer takes two cards from talon and discards two; in unu takes one and discards one; in solo talon stays unseen. Kings, skiz, luna and lowest trump (I) cannot be discarded.
5. Announcements: Declarer speaks first, then anticlockwise. Players may declare trump count (8, 9, or 10+ taroace) and announce bonuses (trula, trump-I-ultimo, rege ultimo, valat, etc.); contra and recontra apply.
6. Play: Player to dealer's right leads. Follow suit; must play a tarok if unable to follow; if tarok is led, must play tarok if possible. Trick won by highest tarok, or highest of led suit. Winner leads next. Twelve tricks.
7. Scoring: Each team counts card points in tricks won; declarer's team needs 36+ to win the game. Bonuses (trula, trump-I-ultimo, etc.) scored per payment table.
keyRules: Follow suit; must play a tarok if you cannot follow suit.
If a tarok is led, you must play a tarok if you can.
Trick is won by the highest tarok in it, or if no tarok, by the highest card of the suit led.
Declarer's team needs at least 36 of 70 card points to win the game.

strategy.basic: Follow suit and trump when required. Lead low trumps to signal holding skiz or luna; lead high trumps (X or above) to show you lack the top two.
strategy.intermediate: Count card points and trumps. In bidding, assess hand strength for doi versus solo. As declarer, choose talon level to balance gain versus loss multiplier.
strategy.advanced: Signal to partner via trump leads. Announce pagat ultimo or rege ultimo when hand supports it. Use contra strategically to double stakes.
tips: Leading a small tarok (below X) conventionally signals you hold skiz or luna.
Declarer's team needs 36 of 70 points; count in threes and subtract 2 per group.

list.name: Taper (three players)
list.description: Three-player form. 42-card pack (remove lowest three cards of each suit). No king called; declarer always plays alone against two in partnership. Twelve cards each, 6 to talon. Lowest bid unul de trei (take three from talon). Declarations 10, 11 or 12 taroace. No rege ultimo; no michi-michi (if all pass, cards thrown in and radler of three hands at double stakes).
list.emptyOverridesReason: Taper uses different deck and no call-king; engine overrides to be added when variant is implemented.

list.name: Michi-michi
list.description: Played when all four players pass. Talon set aside; twelve tricks under usual rules but objective is to avoid winning tricks. No card points, declarations or bonuses. Each player pays one game point to the pool per trick won. Next four hands played at double stakes (radler).
list.emptyOverridesReason: Michi-michi has different objective and scoring; overrides to be added when variant is implemented.

difficulty.easy: Legal follow-suit and trump only. Random bid when holding moderate hand.
difficulty.medium: Count trumps and card points. Bid doi with strong hand, solo with very strong. Basic trump signalling.
difficulty.hard: Full point and trump counting. Optimal talon level choice. Pagat ultimo and rege ultimo announcement when justified. Contra timing.

considerations: Partnership is hidden until called king is played or revealed; AI must not leak partner identity.
70 card points total; counting in threes minus 2 per group; declarer needs 36+.
Bidding has multiple levels in doi/unu affecting loss multiplier only.

engine.deckDescription: A 54-card Industrie und Glück tarock deck with 21 numbered trumps plus the Skus and 32 suit cards. Black suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, 10, 9, 8, 7; red suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, Ace, 2, 3, 4.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits are divided into black suits (Spades and Clubs) and red suits (Hearts and Diamonds), each with its own reduced pip sequence.
engine.rankDescription: Courts are King, Queen, Cavalier, and Jack. Black suits continue with 10, 9, 8, 7; red suits continue with Ace, 2, 3, 4. Trumps run from 1 to 21 plus the Skus.
